_note: SUGGESTIONS, WITH A DECISION GATE. Nothing here is implemented by this session.
Each row states the problem, the evidence that the problem is real, the paths available and what each one costs.
check.py fails the build if any suggestion in this file carries an Approved/Rejected/Implemented status or a chosen_option while its status is still Proposed -
so 'review and choose before implementing' is enforced by the repository, not by good intentions.

Rows marked new_this_cycle arose from this cycle's capture; the rest are carried forward from the two open boards (hub, decision_lab) with their IDs in relates_to, so nothing is silently dropped when a path is chosen.

Impact fields added 2026-11-13: source_ids (registered evidence), moves (what changes on the pages), unblocks (questions this decision answers), closes (flags it retires), related_questions, affects_pages (files inside desk/), enables (features that become possible). check.py validates every id in these lists against the registers, so the impact column cannot cite something that does not exist.

decision_gate.rule: No suggestion may be implemented, and no decision_status may advance past Proposed, until the repository owner records a choice: decision_status plus the exact chosen_option text plus decision_date in this file, and a matching entry in desk/data/decisions.json. desk/check.py fails the build on any state without a record, on any record without a state, on 'Implemented' (the desk builds pages, it does not ship code), and on an impact graph that cites a question, flag or page which does not exist.
decision_gate.enforced_by: desk/check.py (R8 gate, R16 impact graph, R17 decision log)
decision_gate.how_to_change: run: python3 desk/decide.py K04 A --date 2026-11-14 --note 'why', then python3 desk/build.py && python3 desk/check.py

suggestions.title: Name one canonical surface and make the other eight say what they are
suggestions.problem: Ten published surfaces overlap and none is designated authoritative; this desk is a ninth tree, which is the cost of leaving the question open. Upstream suggestions S01 and S14 (decision_lab) and the hub's register are the same ask, still unchosen.
suggestions.evidence: Counted from the tree: git ls-files '*index.html' returns 11 landing pages; flags F12 records it this cycle.

options.option: A. Desk becomes the cycle surface
options.implications: desk/ holds the current-week tables; every other tree is marked 'prior cycle' in its own header by one edit each, no content moved.

options.option: B. hub stays canonical, desk is folded into it
options.implications: One dashboard to maintain, but hub's generator is another session's scope and the merge is a rebuild of 25 pages.

options.option: C. Leave it
options.implications: Cheapest now, most expensive per reading: every future session adds a tree and every reader re-derives which page to trust.

suggestions.recommendation: A, because it costs one banner per tree and stops the count growing. It is not a merge and destroys nothing.
suggestions.relates_to: decision_lab S01, S14; hub register Q14
suggestions.missing_information: The owner's choice of a front door. Nothing else needs to be discovered to make it.

moves: every page header states which surface is authoritative, so a reader cannot mistake this cycle for the current one
the nine trees keep their content but gain one banner line each
enables: a stable URL a decision memo can point at

suggestions.title: Make bye weeks a first-class input of the coverage gate
suggestions.problem: A partial capture and a bye look identical in the injury report. The previous cycle recorded four clubs as unexplained absences; today the official scores page names all four as on bye (flag F01).
suggestions.evidence: A05 'Teams on Bye' section read 2026-11-13; A03 states the slate is 14 games.

options.option: A. Read the bye list from the scores page each cycle and assert 14+4 = 32
options.implications: Two-line change in the capture script; the gate then fails on a real gap instead of a scheduled absence.

options.option: B. Derive byes from the schedule and check club count
options.implications: Stronger, needs a schedule parser per club, which has no machine-readable official endpoint.

options.option: C. Keep flagging absent clubs as unverified
options.implications: Safe, but every bye week produces four false alarms that train people to ignore the gate.

suggestions.recommendation: A, with the raw 'Teams on Bye' line stored verbatim beside the derived list so the assertion is auditable.
suggestions.missing_information: Nothing. This is implementable from an official page that already exists.

moves: the coverage gate counts byes before it counts an absence as a gap, so 32/32 becomes structural instead of a flag
availability.html states the bye list as an input, not as a finding
enables: a Monday-night pipeline that does not fire on an idle club

suggestions.title: Decide how policy currency is established before any rule-dependent field is trusted
suggestions.problem: The definitions that make a blank Game Status meaningful come from an official page with no date line (flag F02). Right now each session decides on its own whether that is good enough.
suggestions.evidence: A06 body read 2026-11-13; no dated policy document was retrieved by this or the previous session.

options.option: A. Accept the league's own article, with a caveat rendered on every page that uses it
options.implications: What this desk does. Honest, and it keeps the caveat where the reader needs it.

options.option: B. Require a dated primary document (bylaws/memo) and leave the field blank until one is found
options.implications: Cleanest evidentially; blocks any use of blank-vs-designation semantics, which is most of the injury signal.

options.option: C. Treat designation semantics as unverified and never derive a feature from them
options.implications: Safest for a model; discards the one place the report is genuinely informative.

suggestions.recommendation: A now and B as a standing task: an owner decision about the evidence bar for rules is worth recording once and applying everywhere.
suggestions.missing_information: A dated, official statement of the injury-report policy in force for 2026, or the league's Game Operations Manual section that contains it.

moves: designation definitions carry an effective date or are marked undated, and the desk stops treating an undated rule as current
the reading of a blank game status becomes an explicit assumption rather than an inference
enables: any rule that reads a designation, including the 0.45 practice-adjustment rule the sibling session proposed

suggestions.title: Acquire an ordered depth source, officially, or stop describing the requirement as met
suggestions.problem: The brief asks the system to know which backup replaces a starter. No official publisher provides depth ordering (flag F03, re-probed today). The requirement is currently met only by a coach sentence in a news article.
suggestions.evidence: A08 returns 404; A10 returns 500; DS4 (club roster) publishes membership and status with no ordering; DS6 (third-party charts) is rejected.

options.option: A. Licence or contract a depth source and put it in the same pinned, hashed pipeline as the odds data
options.implications: Real solution; cost, terms review, and a second provenance chain to verify.

options.option: B. Capture each club's own depth-chart page weekly with a timestamp and treat club pages as official-club tier
options.implications: Free and official-ish; needs a club-by-club URL register, an update-cadence check and a decision that club domains count (governance question still open as decision_lab Q15/S13).

options.option: C. Publish vacancies without fills
options.implications: What this desk does. Honest, and it makes the missing input visible to the person who can fund it.

options.option: D. Declare the requirement out of scope
options.implications: Also legitimate: it says the system will not model replacement quality at all.

suggestions.recommendation: B for the four clubs in the immediately upcoming fixture list first, measured for two weeks, then a decision on scaling. C in the meantime.
suggestions.relates_to: decision_lab S04, Q04; hub depth register
suggestions.missing_information: Whether member-club pages count as official publishers repository-wide, and a per-club register of depth-chart URLs with last-updated evidence.

moves: the depth-string column on depth.html can stop being blank for the clubs captured at kickoff
the brief's 2nd/3rd/4th-string requirement can be described as met rather than as attempted
enables: the depth half of the injury signal

suggestions.title: Define a labelled depth proxy so the gap degrades safely instead of silently
suggestions.problem: With no ordering, the nearest computable statement of replacement quality is 'who is left at that position'. If it is not defined as a proxy, some future model will use it as if it were a depth chart.
suggestions.evidence: A01 rows carry position codes and game statuses; that is enough for the proxy and not enough for a chart.

options.option: A. Proxy = highest-listed player at the position on the club roster page who is not OUT or DOUBTFUL, labelled 'proxy, unordered source'
options.implications: Reproducible, fails loudly when a whole group is OUT, and never claims ordering. Requires a roster parser.

options.option: B. Proxy = count-based only (number of available players at the position, no ordering)
options.implications: Weaker but immune to the ordering fallacy; publishable today from data this desk already captures.

options.option: C. No proxy
options.implications: Cleanest evidentially; the vacancy stays a boolean.

suggestions.recommendation: B now, A only if K04 option B is approved, because A inherits the ordering assumption the roster page does not support.
suggestions.missing_information: Nothing to discover; it is a choice about how much inference is allowed.

moves: depth.html gains a labelled proxy column with its recipe printed next to it, and every proxy cell is visually distinct from an official one
the risk of a proxy being read as fact is priced in rather than denied
enables: a degraded but honest version of the depth feature

suggestions.title: Namespace strategy IDs and gate IDs before any reward is attached to them
suggestions.problem: 15 strategy IDs name different rules in two ledgers and the gate keys G1..G9 mean different things in three systems (flags F08 and the note on desk/gates.html). A leaderboard that pays by ID can pay the wrong entry, and nothing in CI prevents it.
suggestions.evidence: Recomputed this cycle by desk/build_ledger.py from the two artifacts; the collision table is published on desk/signals.html.

options.option: A. Introduce 'family::id' keys (e.g. pipeline::S14, docs::S14) and a compatibility view for old pages
options.implications: Breaks nothing that reads by name; needs one migration commit in each generator's scope, so it is an integration task, not a desk task.

options.option: B. Add a verifier that fails when the same ID carries different names across artifacts, and rename nothing
options.implications: Catches new collisions immediately and costs one check function. Does not fix the old pages.

options.option: C. Rename in place
options.implications: Cheapest to write, worst to audit: it rewrites other sessions' published history and their checks.

suggestions.recommendation: B this cycle, A at the next integration. Both before rewards exist, because the cost of a mispaid reward is that the leaderboard stops being evidence.
suggestions.relates_to: upstream flag X01 (still open); decision_lab S07 (reward form)
suggestions.missing_information: Whether the owner wants one strategy registry object (with families as attributes) rather than three ledgers plus a mapping.

moves: 15 colliding strategy IDs become one identifier per rule, so a leaderboard row names exactly one thing
gate names stop being three different G1-G8 vocabularies
enables: any reward keyed to a strategy ID

suggestions.title: Stamp every captured field with its publication moment, not the capture moment
suggestions.problem: Club records disagreed between two official pages because the Thursday game finished in between (flag F06). A capture timestamp alone cannot express 'as of'.
suggestions.evidence: A03 prints 2-5-1 for Washington; A01 read later the same day prints 3-5-1; A05 gives the final score.

options.option: A. Per-page 'as_printed' field captured with the row
options.implications: Makes cross-page contradictions resolvable by ordering instead of by judgement.

options.option: B. Wednesday, Thursday and Friday snapshots of the same week
options.implications: Turns status changes into observed events (which is what the injury signal actually is) at three times the capture cost.

options.option: C. Keep a single snapshot
options.implications: Cheapest, and it permanently forfeits the intra-week movement that the user's brief describes as the system's edge.

suggestions.recommendation: A now, B if the injury-based signal family is to be developed at all.
suggestions.missing_information: The league's own publication schedule for each report day (Wednesday/Thursday/Friday deadlines and the final inactive list), which no official page states in a retrievable form.

moves: every field carries the moment the publisher printed it, so the report/article record gap stops being a contradiction
reconcile.html's verdict column changes meaning: disagreements become as-of differences or real errors

suggestions.title: Score the leaderboard on the null, not on the headline ROI
suggestions.problem: The repository's own luck band says a best-of-11 selection from the priced ATS pool averages +5.45% ROI, 5th-95th percentile -0.35% to +16.28%, purely from noise. A reward for 'top strategy' pays that noise.
suggestions.evidence: line_lab/data/derived/summary.json extras.luck_band (2,000 simulations, seed 20261101) and the per-row shrunk ROI in data/derived/gates_results.csv (S14 raw +8.41% becomes +2.48% after shrinkage).

options.option: A. Rank by shrunk ROI with the permutation percentile as an eligibility filter
options.implications: Uses what already exists in the artifacts; no new statistic to defend.

options.option: B. Rank by CLV against the close, with results as a tiebreak
options.implications: The standard skill proxy; needs prices at bet time and at close for every fixture, which the pinned dataset does have for closings but not for the model's own quotes.

options.option: C. Rank by both, publish both, refuse to rank by raw ROI
options.implications: More columns, fewer arguments. Recommended.

options.option: D. Keep raw ROI
options.implications: Fastest to build and it will reward the luckiest rule of 2024.

suggestions.relates_to: hub competition page (promotion gates, unfunded rewards); decision_lab S07
suggestions.missing_information: An agreed forward window (how many weeks, which fixtures) before which no ranking is published at all.

moves: the leaderboard re-ranks on shrinkage and calibration instead of headline ROI; the current top signal's +8.41% becomes +2.48% on the published scale
strategies that only look good because of how many were tried stop ranking
enables: a ranking that means something to a bettor
the luck-removal requirement in the brief

suggestions.title: Keep the reward non-monetary until the lawful-and-funded question is answered
suggestions.problem: There is no funded pool and no legal review. reports/leaderboard.json records reward_units 0.0 for all 15 rows and verified/data/leaderboard.json refuses to score at all.
suggestions.evidence: Both artifacts read this cycle; a prior session published the same finding with an unfunded structure.

options.option: A. Non-monetary rewards only: compute priority, a published seed, first claim on forward-book allocation
options.implications: Nothing to licence, nothing to pay, still a leaderboard.

options.option: B. Propose a funded pool and route it to a jurisdiction/legal review before any figure exists
options.implications: Answers Q09 upstream; slow, and the review is outside this repository.

options.option: C. Silent
options.implications: Leaves a leaderboard that implies a prize nobody approved.

suggestions.recommendation: A. No amount is proposed anywhere in desk/, and none should be until B's review exists.
suggestions.relates_to: decision_lab S07, Q09; hub competition page
suggestions.missing_information: Who may lawfully offer a prize for this activity, in the owner's jurisdiction, and whether any pool exists.

moves: the reward column publishes what is actually on offer, and the two ledger surfaces stop disagreeing about whether a reward exists
the competition can run while the legality question stays open, without the site claiming a payout
enables: a public competition with a defined prize

suggestions.title: Publish parlays and prop combos as their own tested objects, never as arithmetic on singles
suggestions.problem: The measured same-game dependence is far below what a two-leg ticket needs, and no official source publishes prop lines to test props against. Combining legs is therefore not a smaller risk than it looks, and props cannot be validated at all today.
suggestions.evidence: desk/signals.html correlation section: recomputed phi for the three published same-game pairs matches the ledger (+0.0161 spread x total; +0.6706 spread x ML, which is the dependence a ticket is not supposed to contain); required 2-leg breakeven phi 0.0975; cross-game mean phi -0.0239; pipeline signal_matrix median |phi| across 93 evaluable cross-market pairs 0.0458. props: player_log_present false, prop_lines_present false.

options.option: A. Allow only cross-game, uncorrelated parlays; block same-game spread+ML
options.implications: Directly supported by the measured phi and by the fact that spread x ML is where the dependence actually lives.

options.option: B. Price the ticket from the legs and test the parlay as its own strategy with its own gates
options.implications: Correct but data-hungry: needs every leg's price at bet time.

options.option: C. No parlays until props and parlay settlement are sourceable
options.implications: Removes the temptation; loses a use case the brief asks for.

options.option: D. Allow props on projected-received stats only
options.implications: Prop format is the only one a model can validate without official lines - and it still has no price to beat.

suggestions.recommendation: A plus C for props, with B queued behind the price-source question. The correlation arithmetic is already in the repository; the missing thing is prices and settlement rules, not analysis.
suggestions.missing_information: Any machine-readable price source for player props, and an official or operator statement of push/void settlement for a leg inside a parlay.

moves: parlays and prop combos appear as tested objects with their own gate results, not as a sum of single-bet numbers
the correlation table becomes load-bearing: a two-leg ticket at breakeven needs mean pairwise correlation below 0.0975

suggestions.title: Build the capture as an event log so 'changed' is a measured quantity
suggestions.problem: Injuries move markets on the announcement, not on the absence. A once-a-week snapshot cannot see an announcement, and no session has been able to measure movement because nothing was stored between reads.
suggestions.evidence: This cycle: the Friday roundup ruled a Texan out while the report and the article both said questionable (desk/reconcile.html N01). That is an announcement the table never showed.

options.option: A. Append-only capture per club-week with source URL and page text hash
options.implications: Makes change detection possible and gives every published row a stable audit handle.

options.option: B. Continue replacing files each cycle
options.implications: Simple, and it guarantees the most valuable field - the change - stays unmeasurable.

options.option: C. A nightly job with a retained diff
options.implications: Same benefit, needs an owner for the runner and a rule for what counts as a change.

suggestions.recommendation: A. It is cheap now and impossible later; the brief's 'no manual input' requirement cannot be satisfied by a hand-refreshed snapshot either way.
suggestions.missing_information: Permission/feasibility of scheduled fetches from the owner's side, since this sandbox has no egress to nfl.com and every capture is a session-time read.

moves: capture becomes an append-only event log, so 'the report changed' is a measured quantity with a distribution instead of an anecdote
the 160-row snapshot table is replaced by transitions with timestamps

suggestions.title: State a pre-mortem next to every strategy, and publish the killed ones
suggestions.problem: Eighteen signals tested and none passed; the results that failed are the most informative content in the repository and they are scattered across three ledgers.
suggestions.evidence: Consolidated on desk/signals.html: 11 line_lab strategies, 18 pipeline signals, 15 ranked docs rows, 8 not-eligible workbench rows - zero eligible in every ledger.

options.option: A. One row per strategy across all builds with its failing gate and a one-sentence pre-mortem
options.implications: Turns four ledgers into a research record; the desk page is already this shape and could be extended in place.

options.option: B. Keep per-build pages as they are
options.implications: Preserves each session's framing but keeps the 'we tried this and it failed' signal invisible.

options.option: C. Publish only survivors
options.implications: Guarantees the next session re-tests what already failed, which is how 18 signals became 36.

suggestions.missing_information: Nothing to discover; it is a presentation choice with a real research cost attached.

moves: each strategy carries the condition under which it would have been killed before promotion, and the killed list is published next to the survivors

suggestions.title: Add the per-row player-page verification this desk could only sample
suggestions.problem: The brief requires every row to be verified against an official source. This desk links every row to the page it came from and spot-verified one row against the player's own official page; 159 of 160 designation rows carry a link nobody re-opened.
suggestions.evidence: A07 confirms position, club and status for one captured row. The method and its limit are printed in meta.json's transcription_policy.

options.option: A. Verify every row's player page in the next cycle and record the field-by-field match
options.implications: About 160 page reads per cycle: expensive in a session, cheap as a scheduled job - and it is the only way 'verified line by line' is literally true.

options.option: B. Verify a fixed random sample per cycle and publish the sample rate
options.implications: Honest and affordable; states a confidence instead of implying completeness.

options.option: C. Keep the link-only standard
options.implications: What most pages in this repository actually meet; the word 'verified' should then be reserved for recomputation, not for provenance.

suggestions.recommendation: B now, A when K11's event log exists, because an append-only capture makes re-verification incremental.
suggestions.missing_information: Whether the owner wants session time spent on verification depth or on signal breadth - this is a budget decision, not a data one.

moves: the sampled 1-of-160 verification becomes a per-row check of identity, position and roster status, with failures flagged instead of assumed
club-code joins get a tested mapping, which is where the historical dataset currently breaks

suggestions.title: Add an 'act on this?' header to data pages, with the date and the blocking flags
suggestions.problem: The site is read as if it were live odds. It is not, and the strongest evidence for that - open flags, unmet gates - is on a different page.
suggestions.evidence: Upstream suggestion decision_lab S12 proposed the same banner; the desk's pages carry an inline status strip computed from flags.json rather than typed.

options.option: A. Status strip on every page: capture date, count of open high-severity flags, whether any strategy is eligible
options.implications: Self-updating from data, cannot go stale, no manual editing.

options.option: B. A single banner on the landing page
options.implications: Easier, and it is what the root site already does; readers scroll past it.

options.option: C. Nothing
options.implications: Leaves the misreading risk where it is today.

suggestions.missing_information: Nothing. It is a template change inside whichever surface wins K01.

moves: each data page leads with the date, the count, and the flags that make acting on it unsafe today
enables: a reader who can tell 'no decision possible' from 'a decision is waiting'

impact_legend: Read the 'State' column first: every row on this page is a proposal, so the consequences described under 'If chosen' are what the desk would do, not what it has done. The references in these columns are checked by desk/check.py - a question, flag or page named here has to exist in the registers, and a decision that claims to retire a flag has to be recorded in decisions.json before the flag may move out of the open count.
